prompt:
Scene:
A square photograph at dusk with a 50mm full-frame camera, positioned on a ridge looking across an active volcanic caldera. Warm twilight with visible heat shimmer over the crater.

Subject:
Instead of lava flowing down the volcano's flanks, rivers of molten lava climb upward from the caldera rim, forming glowing vertical tendrils that rise 400 meters and slowly cool into dark igneous strands at the top. Steam rises alongside the lava in the normal direction, creating a strange upward-upward dual system.

Important details:
Physically believable lava appearance: orange-yellow hot interior, darker skin forming at the surface, small detachment drips behaving in the inverted direction (dripping upward). Strong thermal gradient in the air distorts the background mountains into wavering silhouettes. A vulcanologist in reflective suit stands at the rim as a 1.8-meter scale anchor. Sulfur-tinted sky fades from peach to deep indigo.

Use case:
Lift-studies single 2/5 — reverse gravity applied to molten material in a volcanic context.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no branded safety suits, no helicopters, no dragons, no cartoon stylization, no CGI polygon edges on the lava.
